advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Paginate `get_issuelinks_map`/`get_comment_map` over the whole project (loop `search_issues` with advancing `start_at` until a short page) instead of a single default-50 call.
evidence: transport.py:260 `issues = self.search_issues(f"project = {project_key}")` — no start_at/max_results, no loop
transport.py:274 `issues = self.search_issues(f"project = {project_key}")` in get_comment_map
`_backend.py:97-99` the protocol signature `search_issues(self, jql, start_at=0, max_results=50)` — a page slice callers paginate

Cloud equivalents page the whole project: acli_graph.py:382 `get_issuelinks_map ... via ONE paged REST search` with `while True:`/`nextPageToken` (lines 410-420) and acli_graph.py:280 `get_comment_map ... paged`
fetcher.py:534 `issuelinks_map = client.get_issuelinks_map(project_key)` and fetcher.py:497 `comment_map = client.get_comment_map(project_key)` consume these as project-wide bulk maps
ABSENCE: the unit-test fake `search_issues` ignores paging kwargs and returns everything (test_jira_dc_transport.py:69-70), so no test exercises >50 issues
advisory.finding: `get_issuelinks_map` and `get_comment_map` call `search_issues(f"project = {project_key}")` a single time with the default `max_results=50` and no pagination loop, so for a project with more than 50 issues they silently return link/comment data for only the first 50 — the fetcher then enriches only those, dropping the rest.
scenarios: A DC project with >50 issues: inbound link sync and comment dedup see stale/empty data for issues past the first page, causing missed inbound links and re-emitted comments each pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a helper that loops `search_issues(jql, start_at=n, max_results=100)` accumulating until a returned page is shorter than max_results, and use it in both map builders.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test that a non-loopback `http://` `reconciler.base_url` with `allow_insecure=False` raises `ConfigError`, and a second asserting the `allow_insecure=True` override path logs the cleartext-risk warning.
evidence: src/rebar/_config_schema.py:98 `if not allow_insecure:` -> `raise ConfigError(...)` — the reject branch
ABSENCE: search of tests/ for `reconciler.base_url`, `cleartext`, and `not 'https'` returns no matches
tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py:92 `allow_insecure=True` with settings built directly (fixture bypasses load_config), so `_validate_reconciler_tls` never runs in the live tier

Ticket 9fd4 AC: 'the DC backend REJECTS a non-https reconciler.base_url with a ConfigError ...; a unit test covers the reject branch with a non-loopback http:// URL, and a second test asserts the override path emits a warning naming the risk'
advisory.finding: The security-critical reject branch of `_validate_reconciler_tls` — a non-`https` `reconciler.base_url` with `allow_insecure=False` raising `ConfigError` — has no test in any tier. The heldout suite only asserts the client-construction `options['verify']` value, never the config validator; the live suite explicitly sets `allow_insecure=True` and builds `JiraDataCenterSettings` directly (bypassing `load_config`/`__post_init__`), so the validator is never exercised. A regression that dropped or weakened the https requirement (the exact 'fail open silently' risk the validator guards) would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: In a config-schema unit test, construct a `ReconcilerConfig(base_url='http://jira.internal.example', allow_insecure=False)` and assert `pytest.raises(ConfigError)`; then construct with `allow_insecure=True` and assert `caplog` captures the warning naming the risk.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Apply `_validate_project_key` (or an equivalent project-key regex) to `project_key` before interpolating it into JQL in the DC transport's `get_issuelinks_map`/`get_comment_map`, matching the injection-safety guard used by `jql_active`/`jql_done_recent`.
evidence: transport.py:260 `issues = self.search_issues(f"project = {project_key}")`
transport.py:274 `issues = self.search_issues(f"project = {project_key}")`

fetcher.py:54-66 `_validate_project_key` — docstring: 'Guards both correctness ... and JQL-injection safety (the key is interpolated unquoted into the JQL).' with regex `_PROJECT_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$")`

fetcher.py:443 `project_key = _query_project` (config `query_project`, i.e. `jira.project`) with fallback to a snapshot-derived key; passed straight through backend.py:227/269 to the transport with no validation
_config_schema.py coercion table: `"base_url": lambda v, k: _as_str(v, k)` and `jira.project` is `_as_str` only — no project-key regex is applied at the coercion layer either
ABSENCE: no call to `_validate_project_key` (or equivalent regex check) exists anywhere on the DC path (backend.py:226-227, 268-269; transport.py:259-263, 273-280)
advisory.finding: The DC transport interpolates `project_key` directly into a JQL string (`search_issues(f"project = {project_key}")`) in `get_issuelinks_map` and `get_comment_map` without applying the codebase's established `_validate_project_key` guard, which fetcher.py documents as existing specifically for 'JQL-injection safety'. `project_key` reaches these methods from config-derived `jira.project` (coerced only by `_as_str`, no key-shape regex) or from snapshot-derived keys, so a malformed/hostile project key is interpolated unquoted into the query language sink.
scenarios: A `[tool.rebar.jira].project` / `JIRA_PROJECT` value containing JQL metacharacters (spaces, `OR`, quotes) is interpolated unquoted into the `project = <key>` clause, broadening or altering the search beyond the intended project scope.
The snapshot-derived fallback key path passes a server-returned key fragment into the same unquoted JQL sink.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `get_issuelinks_map`/`get_comment_map`, validate `project_key` against the same `_PROJECT_KEY_RE` (or reuse `fetcher._validate_project_key`) before building `f"project = {project_key}"`, so a malformed key is rejected fail-closed rather than interpolated into JQL.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (or document) that retrying connection-level faults on non-idempotent `create_issue`/`add_comment` cannot duplicate, given the HTTP-error path is explicitly unretried for exactly that duplicate risk.
evidence: transport.py:195 `issue = _with_connection_retry(lambda: self._client.create_issue(**fields))`
transport.py:270 `comment = _with_connection_retry(lambda: self._client.add_comment(remote_id, body))`

transport.py:134-137 docstring: HTTP error 'propagates on the FIRST attempt, unretried ... (retrying a mutation on an HTTP error risks duplicates)' — but a connection Timeout on the same mutation carries the identical duplicate risk and IS retried
dropped.finding: `create_issue` and `add_comment` (non-idempotent mutations) are wrapped in `_with_connection_retry`, which retries connection-level faults; a timeout after the server accepted the request will re-issue the create/comment and duplicate it — the very risk the code cites to justify NOT retrying HTTP errors.
scenarios: A read-timeout raised after Jira processed a create/comment but before the response was read: the retry creates a second issue or duplicate comment.
